summary: A Q&A thread asks whether being bad at maths indicates low IQ, prompted by a successful business master's student who struggles with algebra, geometry and statistics but handles financial equations well and was told by an acquaintance that poor maths signals low IQ. Respondents give mixed views: many argue IQ and maths ability are separate, citing Einstein's self-described math difficulties, dyscalculia, and the fact that IQ tests emphasize pattern and logical reasoning; a few argue poor maths reflects lack of practice or motivation and matters for business careers. The page is a clipped Narkive/Yahoo Answers archive with navigation and site boilerplate ignored.
one_line: Online Q&A thread debating whether poor maths ability indicates low IQ, with answers citing Einstein, dyscalculia and IQ test design.
key_facts: The original question asks: "Is being bad at maths a sign of a low IQ?" and was posted on 2020-11-23.
The original poster is doing a master's of business management at a leading university and has come first in two subjects.
The original poster barely passed stats but has always been shockingly horrible at maths, especially algebra, geometry, and stats, though they are ok with financial equations.
The original poster dropped maths in the final year of high school, which they say is allowed in Australia.
A successful acquaintance argued that being bad at maths is a sign of low IQ because maths is essentially logic.
One answer quotes Einstein: "Do not worry about your difficulties in Mathematics. I can assure you mine are still greater."
The answer says Einstein is thought to have had a 160 IQ and that his teachers thought he wasn't trying when he was a boy.
One answer claims Richard Feynman was supposed to have a 126 IQ because he wasn't so good at "English".
A respondent who identifies as a theoretical physicist says some people are "bad at math" while having excellent language skills.
A respondent says dyscalculia is the mathematical equivalent of dyslexia and is not indicative of intelligence.
The answer on IQ tests states that a quality IQ test gauges a person's ability to discern patterns and is not a trivia test or a math test.
A respondent who taught math as an adjunct found many students struggling with calculus did well in other subjects such as organic chemistry.
One respondent says maths is essential to business because maximizing profit requires math.
Another respondent says math weaknesses early on will haunt a learner for the rest of their mathematical career unless they relearn it from scratch.
